item.title: Nex 2.2.2
item.description: The portrait arrives as you scroll. Each part of your writing portrait — the figures, the 30-day bars, the ring, the shape of your traits — now plays its entrance when you scroll to it, instead of everything finishing the moment the page opens. The page also opens lighter, so the small stutter on entering is gone. A different "One thing to try" each time. Writing the portrait again used to give the same suggestion over and over. Nex now remembers the last few it gave and steers the next one to a different area.

item.title: Nex 2.2.1
item.description: One Nex card in recent apps. After updating and tapping Open in the installer, Nex could appear twice in the recent-apps list — one card for the old window, one for the new. Nex now rejoins its own window instead of starting a second one. Safer sponsor card. The sponsor picture is only fetched over a secure connection and never from an address on your own network. A long library stays quick. After scrolling deep into thousands of notes and coming back to the top, Nex lets go of the extra depth it had loaded, so adding or editing a note no longer re-reads everything you scrolled through. Less memory with the on-device model. The on-device search model is now let go before the on-device chat model loads, and also when Android asks for memory, so a phone with little spare memory is less likely to close Nex.

item.title: Nex 2.2.0
item.description: Set aside. Hold a note and choose Set aside to take it off the home screen without deleting it. Pick when it comes back — this evening, tomorrow morning, next week, a date — or leave it until you bring it back yourself. Set-aside notes wait in Library → Set aside , where one tap brings a note home; search still finds them, marked, and their reminders still ring. It is also in a note's details and in the bar for several selected notes. A banner offers Undo , and when a chosen date arrives the note returns by itself and says so. With everything set aside, the home screen says All clear instead of asking for a first note. Bank cards, reworked. The "Continue unfinished edit" notice no longer appears when you opened a card and changed nothing, or opened a new one and typed nothing — it appears only after a real change, and goes away if you undo it. A card number is kept if it has 12–19 digits, from any bank in any country: a last digit that does not match only shows a note under the field, so a number like 6104 3378 3546 8074 can be saved. Under the number Nex names the card network when it can (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, UnionPay, JCB, Diners Club, Maestro, Mir, Troy, RuPay). Numbers are grouped as on the card as you type, Persian digits are converted, Iranian banks are recognised from the first digits and fill the Bank field when it is empty, the IBAN is shown in groups, and an expiry may be month/year or year/month. A tapped reminder, when Nex was closed. The scroll to the note and the blink around it now wait until the app has settled — and until you have unlocked it, if the app lock is on — so you see them instead of missing them behind the opening. Your writing portrait, more alive. The card now assembles itself when you scroll to it: the numbers count up, the busiest part of your day grows, the last 30 days rise as bars (today on the end), what you keep fills a ring, and a written portrait's traits draw a shape you can read at a glance. It also shows your current streak of days with a note and your longest run. Write again is always there once the portrait is unlocked; without an AI provider it tells you where to choose one, instead of being missing. Modules, paused for now. Habits, Price Lens, Lent & Borrowed, Quit Habits, Birthdays & occasions, Expenses, Gold, Words, Parking, Medicine, Warranty and Maintenance are marked Soon again while they are finished properly. Only Cycle stays available. Nothing you saved in them is touched, and they come back when they are ready.

item.title: Nex 2.1.15
item.description: One menu everywhere. The ⋮ menus on threads, tags, the modules and the rest now look and size like the menu you get by holding a card — rounded, an icon on every line, delete in red — and so do the dropdown lists in forms.

item.title: Nex 2.1.14
item.description: Shorter forms. Adding an occasion, a medicine, a purchase, an asset, a parking or a loan now asks only the essentials; the rest (a year, a note, a reminder, a brand, coordinates, dates…) waits behind one "more details" button, and opens by itself when you edit something saved. A face for every module. Each module's page now opens with one large, calm statement in its own colour — "12 days free", "2/3 checked today", the gold estimate, what is due — instead of a plain list. Quit Habits asks less. A new habit asks only what you are quitting and when it started. The amounts, price, goal and reason wait behind one button, for whenever you want them. Tap outside to close. Form sheets — adding an occasion, a habit, a payment and the like — now close when you tap the dimmed area above them, like every other sheet. If you have typed something, they still ask before discarding it. Expenses, Gold, Words, Parking, Medicine, Warranty and Maintenance are available. The last seven modules are out of Soon: add them from Tools → Add modules . Each was checked page by page; no new ones are Soon. Dates you type show in your calendar. Where you type a date in a module, a line under it reads that day back in your own calendar (a Jalali reader sees the Jalali date). Expenses shows the Jalali span of the month you are looking at. Pages with nothing yet have one button. The empty Expenses, Words, Parking, Medicine, Warranty and Maintenance pages show a single button instead of a button and a floating one. Forms no longer hide under the keyboard. Every sheet that opens over the keyboard — in the modules and the rest of the app — now lifts above it, so each field can be reached and the form completed. Lent & Borrowed. On the second tab, a swipe returns to the first; the next swipe goes back.

item.title: Nex 2.1.13
item.description: Birthdays & occasions. A new module for the dates you do not want to miss — birthdays, anniversaries, remembrances. Each date repeats in its own calendar, so a Jalali birthday comes back on the same Jalali day every year. You see a countdown, the age it comes to (when you know the year), the day in both calendars, a greeting to copy or share, and an optional reminder ahead of the day. Nothing is sent for you and no contacts are read. Add it from Tools → Add modules . Habits. A calendar of every month, in your own calendar: tap any day up to today to mark it, tap again to take it back. A new How often panel shows the days you kept it out of the days since you started.

item.title: Nex 2.1.10
item.description: YouTube analysis now shows its result. "Analyze video" ran, finished and kept the analysis, but showed nothing: a note's summary is hidden when it is not shorter than the note's own words, and a YouTube link's words are only a title and a line, so every real analysis was hidden. The analysis of a YouTube link now always appears in the note's AI section. More failures are in the diagnostics report. A video that could not be analysed, an AI request the provider refused, a failed backup, export or restore, a photo or recording that could not be saved, a stopped update, a private-area error and a module that could not read or save its records are now written to the local log, which Send feedback and Share diagnostics can attach. Only the kind and status code are written — never an address, a key, a reply or anything from your notes.

item.title: Nex 2.1.9
item.description: Reminders stay until you deal with them. A reminder that has rung now stays in the notification shade until you tap or dismiss it. Opening Nex used to clear them all, because putting every alarm back on launch also took away the ones already showing — repeating reminders, recurring items, Cycle and module reminders and the daily nudge alike. Clearing a reminder or deleting its note still takes its notification away. YouTube analysis that works on real videos. The video is now watched at a lower resolution and half the frame rate — about a fifth of the tokens, still plenty to follow a talk or a tutorial — so a long video no longer runs into a free plan's per-minute limit, and the wait before giving up is longer. The capability check makes the same request, so a check that passes means analysis works. A model or gateway that refuses those settings is asked again the ordinary way. When a video cannot be analysed, Nex says why. The plan's limit, taking too long, Gemini refusing (with its reason and code, such as a private video), or an answer with nothing in it — instead of one sentence for all of them. An analysis that finished is kept even if the page's description arrived meanwhile; it used to be thrown away.

item.title: Nex 2.1.8
item.description: Nex finds out what your AI model can do. Test connection now also checks, with four small test requests, whether the model reads pictures, hears recordings, searches by meaning and watches YouTube videos, and the provider page shows the answer row by row — with the reason when one does not work: the provider has no such service, the model refused, or it could not be checked just then. The three Image input , Transcription and Search embeddings dropdowns are gone; what the check finds decides which features Nex offers. The check sends only test material Nex makes itself — a picture of a number, a second of tone, one sentence and a public YouTube video — never your notes, and runs only when you test. Gemini from a reseller, with everything Gemini can do. Google Gemini now takes an optional Service address : a reseller's or gateway's address in Gemini's own format, with or without /v1beta . Entered there instead of under Custom, the same model can watch YouTube videos and take recordings in Gemini's own way, and the test checks what the reseller passes on. Your key and requests go to that address; only a full https:// address is accepted, outside your own network. Pick a model from your provider's list. The list button in the model field shows the models your key can use, with search, and the field says which model is used when it is left empty. The speech and search model fields are under Speech and search models . New search waits for you. When a check finds that a provider you already use can now search by meaning — OpenRouter, for example — search stays off until you turn it on in Intelligence, because it sends your notes' text to be indexed. Intelligence says why. An ability your provider or model cannot do is greyed with the reason, such as "Anthropic has no speech-to-text service", instead of one general line. The count of working abilities leaves out the paused one, the heading over them says Abilities , the provider row shows the model in use and asks you to test it when its abilities have not been checked yet, and On-device only and Custom read in Persian in Persian. Analyze video is offered only for a Gemini model that can watch videos. Persian digits everywhere. Two dozen counts that still showed Latin digits in Persian — among them the assistant's choice of how many notes it reads — now use Persian digits.

item.title: Nex 2.1.7
item.description: Your writing portrait. At the foot of your profile, once you have 30 notes written on at least 7 days, Nex shows how you write: the part of the day most of your notes come from, how many days you wrote on in the last month, how many checklist items you tick, what kinds of notes you keep and your most used tags — all counted on the phone. Until then, a ring shows how far there is to go. With an AI provider, Write my portrait asks it for a short portrait in words: a headline, a few sentences, five traits with how strongly each shows, your strengths and one thing to try. It reads a sample of up to 80 notes, sent once when you tap, and is a reflection of your notes — not a test or a diagnosis. Analyze a YouTube video. A link note with a YouTube video offers Analyze video in its AI tools when your provider is Gemini: the video itself is watched, and you get what it is about, its main points with their times, and who it is for — instead of a summary of the page's few words. The result is kept as the note's summary. The second line of a compact card is whole again. With compact cards and small or standard text, a two-line note with a reminder or an attachment no longer loses the bottom of its second line, in Persian or any language, whatever the phone's own text size. Pinching the timeline never refreshes it. Folding or opening every day with two fingers no longer sets off pull to refresh when the pinch starts at the top of the list. Privacy, said exactly. Onboarding, the backup screen and the privacy policy now say what a backup protects: settings and service keys are encrypted with your recovery code, the notes are kept as files you can always open. What left this device now names the notes behind the smart summary, the greeting, a translation, a rewrite and the search index, and the notes the assistant read in Recently Deleted. Safer by default. A link preview no longer fetches a page whose name points inside your own network. With the app lock on, Cycle reminders stay off the lock screen like note reminders. Restoring settings from another phone no longer brings a sync server address with it. A complete backup that claims to unpack far larger than it is is refused before anything is written, and deleting a module's data always replaces the older backups on this phone. Small fixes. Daily and weekly recurring items keep their time across a daylight-saving change. The backup just made is never removed by its own rotation when the phone's clock has moved back. Taps in sheets show their ripple again. The photo editor's ratio and colour buttons are full-size and no longer clip with large text, and an annotated photo keeps exactly its original size. Sizes, counts, the voice speed (۱٫۵×) and the annotation slider use Persian digits in Persian. The Cycle widget points to Tools → Modules when Cycle is off. A search you confirm for the assistant always runs, and app questions asked casually ("how's…", «چجوری…») find the guide.

item.title: Nex 2.1.6
item.description: Swipe through a PDF. Pages turn by swiping sideways, the way the interface reads, and the page you are heading for is prepared while you swipe. The slider under the page is gone: a small capsule over the page holds the arrows and the page count, and tapping the count opens a sheet of page numbers to jump straight to one. Double-tap zooms in where you tapped, and a white page now has a visible edge. A smart summary that knows what a reminder is. A reminder you set is said as when to do the thing — "call the plumber tomorrow at 9" — instead of as a deadline counting down hours. Days are counted by the calendar, so a reminder five days away is no longer "four days". The summary never suggests a reminder you already have, and a deadline written in the note itself (such as "until 1405/08/07") is kept apart from the reminder's time; it now knows today's Solar Hijri date to read such dates. The plain report says reminders the same way: "dentist — tomorrow at 09:00". Every summary line alike. Each line's emoji sits in a column of its own with the words lined up beside it, and the first line no longer reads as a heading over the rest. The greeting without a name reads properly. With no name set, "What have you got, ?" is now "What have you got?". Smaller polish. The Nex AI section of a note is a visible card rather than an unexplained indent; the actions and history sheets of a recurring item have the handle, swipe-to-close and glass of every other sheet; a few Persian labels now use one spelling. Gemini works again without a model typed. Nex now uses Google's current Flash model (the gemini-flash-latest alias) when the model field is empty. The previous default, Gemini 2.5 Flash, was retired in October 2026, so a Gemini key with the field left empty could fail on every request. Newer OpenAI models answer. GPT-5 and later reasoning models, including the suggested gpt-6.1-sol , now receive the request format OpenAI requires for them ( max_completion_tokens , no custom temperature) instead of failing on the first message. Sharing into Nex is safe on every Android version. The invisible share window no longer requests a fixed orientation, which Android 8.0 refuses with a crash and which could turn the app you were sharing from. "Save to Nex" from selected text uses the same window. Suggest tags says when there is nothing new. A tap that finds no new tags now explains it instead of appearing to do nothing. Links end where the address ends. Persian written straight after a web address, without a space, is no longer read as part of the domain; Persian paths such as Wikipedia articles still open in full. Tap to pause a video. Tap a playing video to pause it and tap again to resume. Restore a Windows backup without losing the phone's settings. A backup made in Nex for Windows brings back only the shared appearance — theme, accent, language, calendar, text and card size — and leaves this phone's AI keys, private settings and device identity as they were. Exports and imports also find the files of notes and attachments saved on Windows.

item.title: Nex 2.1.5
item.description: Smart summaries refresh automatically only after relevant information changes and at least one hour after the last successful generation. Failed requests wait 15 minutes before retrying; manual refresh remains available immediately. Existing text stays readable, concurrent requests are shared, and every summary line uses the same type size. Show in full appears only when expanding a card reveals more content, taking its width and text size into account. PDF pages stay visible while the next page loads, with a steady viewer height and smoother transitions. A failed page keeps the current page and offers retry. Birthdays & occasions joins the Soon module catalogue, with planned Persian/Gregorian dates, anniversaries, advance reminders and gift notes. Phone screens stay in portrait until the landscape layout is redesigned.

item.title: Nex 2.1.4
item.description: Link cards can now carry photos, recordings and files through Attach, like text notes. Sharing keeps the URL alongside its caption and files. Videos play inside note details in a rounded player, with seeking, speed and mute controls. Playback starts only when requested and pauses when leaving or covering the note. PDFs open inside note details with page navigation, a page slider and pinch or button zoom. PDF and video attachments open in the same detail sheet; Open in another app remains available.

item.title: Nex 2.1.2
item.description: Incomplete AI translations, rewrites and image readings no longer replace complete text; authored markup is preserved. Switching translation language clears the previous result, so a failed request cannot show the wrong language. Assistant questions are saved before waiting; Retry repeats the original question. Cloud responses can be stopped and long conversations use bounded context. Search upgrades rebuild outdated indexed text in batches. Filtered results load in pages, and nearby-match suggestions avoid repeated tag reads. Important handled failures enter bounded, redacted local diagnostics; database errors retain their category across the worker boundary.

item.title: Nex 2.1.0
item.description: Safer AI settings. A delayed connection test cannot save a different provider; a failed credential save keeps the previous setup and reports the failure. Connection-test guidance now distinguishes chat from media and search. Reliable AI requests. Audio deadlines cover the full response, provider errors remain retriable, and switching the search model discards late query vectors. OpenAI o-series requests use their supported token parameter while existing gateway payloads stay unchanged. Orderly on-device answers. Local generation runs one request at a time. Expired work is skipped and late answers are discarded without freeing a native session mid-generation. Accurate assistant state. Output-language changes reach the next chat turn, retired provider connections finish active reads before closing, and Gemini audio is recorded correctly in the local disclosure log. Models and capabilities. Separate speech/search models and custom endpoints, per-model feature controls, and opt-in OpenRouter transcription and embeddings. Manual summaries and tag suggestions can use the downloaded model; capture stays quick. Provider-picker examples are current without replacing saved models. Fresh sponsor cards. Campaigns revalidate hourly on launch/resume; closing a card hides it for eight hours, including across restarts, and it can be closed again when it returns. Complete backups import again. Android can select .nexfull files, and complete backups are recognized even when the document provider renames the selected copy. Clearer reminders. Expanded notifications include up to 1,200 characters. Tapping a reminder scrolls to its card, even beyond the first page, with an outline matching Compact, Standard and Easy Read cards. Cleaner note results. Converting text to a Markdown document no longer presents its source as a Nex AI result. All missed release notes. Updating across several versions shows their changes together, in the selected language. The security toolbox joins Modules as Coming soon.

item.title: Nex 2.0.10
item.description: Custom gateway voice transcription. OpenAI-compatible custom providers with a standard chat endpoint now offer transcription and voice input. Audio is sent to the matching /audio/transcriptions endpoint, leaving chat, images and other providers unchanged.

item.title: Nex 2.0.9
item.description: Softer card changes. Deleted and filtered cards fade and fold away, restored cards settle back in, and pinned notes move between their groups. Unchanged cards keep their state; the list stays lazy and off-screen changes skip the animation. Quiet feedback. Adding a tag or changing a pin gives the card marker a brief pulse. Updated daily briefs blend into their new text, and switching glass on or off uses the same reveal as a theme change. Reduced motion is respected. Clear search indexing. The former Catch up section now explains that it indexes existing note text for semantic search and related notes, up to 25 notes per pass. It does not transcribe audio or read images, and a zero-result pass no longer claims the backlog is complete. On the way: Persian calendar & prayer times. A single coming-soon module groups the Solar Hijri calendar, occasions, date conversion, city-based prayer times and optional adhan alerts.

item.title: Nex 2.0.8
item.description: Smooth focus outlines. Settings search and the assistant composer now keep a continuous rounded focus border in light and dark themes. The main search keeps its blue glow with a softer fade and no clipped rectangle. A livelier assistant wait. While a reply is on its way, a sparkle, thinking text and three gently moving dots replace the empty loading bar. Reduced motion keeps the indicator still.

item.title: Nex 2.0.7
item.description: Accurate result names for files. Cached Markdown and other non-image file text is labelled Extracted text. Image descriptions keep their own title; attached files follow the same rule. Existing content is preserved. Compact AI tools below your note. The AI workspace returns below the content and tags. Its actions, including Suggest tags, use icons with long-press labels, and the result status aligns with the edge. Tidier results, fully hideable. Results have their own reading area and a compact result selector. Hide removes the output and its controls; Show results brings it back without requesting AI again. Text notes keep their own body. Summaries and translations no longer offer Add to caption for text notes. Copy and translation's Save as note remain available. Clearer dialog boundaries. Details, caption confirmation, discard confirmation and other standard dialogs now have a visible theme-matched border and dim the content beneath them in light and dark mode. Glass keeps its existing finish. Orderly caption choices. Append text, Replace caption and Cancel use equally wide buttons with consistent spacing, including Persian and larger text.

item.title: Nex 2.0.6
item.description: Experimental text magnifier. Native Android editing now feeds its selection geometry to Flutter’s built-in magnifier, keeping the app’s surface renderer. Cursor/handle dragging and behavior on individual phones still need real-device testing. AI actions where you can see them. Each note has an AI workspace above its content, with relevant actions, colored icons and readable labels. Results appear in the same place with a short preview, an expandable reading area, and copy or add-to-caption controls. Translation stays alongside other results, with language selection and Save as note. Choose how AI updates a caption. When a caption already exists, choose Cancel, Append or Replace caption. A replacement preserves the original note and media, and refuses to overwrite a caption edited while the confirmation was open. Similar notes paused. The similar-notes section and its lookups are temporarily disabled. Your saved preference is retained; semantic search remains available.

item.title: Nex 2.0.5
item.description: Lighter everyday screens. In-page cards, settings controls, chat bubbles and search keep their glass edges and finish without repeatedly blurring the page behind them. Floating menus, sheets and navigation keep their live glass. Restore the normal Android renderer. The main app no longer renders every page into a texture for the selection magnifier. The native editor still preserves mixed Persian/English paragraphs, formatting and private copying. The Android system magnifier remains a device-validation limitation; this update does not claim to fix it. Less work while writing. Unchanged editor settings and formatting labels are reused across typing and parent rebuilds, without recreating the editor or sending its text back to Android. Clearer AI actions. Image reading, audio transcription and other assistant actions use accent-coloured icons and the theme's normal text colour: dark in light mode, light in dark mode. Destructive and unavailable actions keep their own states.

item.title: Nex 2.0.4
item.description: Selection without keyboard surprises. A small halo around the focused input protects taps near text-selection handles while a farther tap still dismisses the keyboard. Matching context menus. Link Open/Copy uses the card menu's type, icon size, spacing, rounded corners and optional floating glass. Pause is on the way. The module catalog now previews an offline breathing break with calm, focus and relax modes; it is not installed or enabled. AI actions fit the item. Images offer Describe & read image; recordings offer Transcribe audio. Media is read only when requested, including attachments. Translate and Summarize operate on suitable text rather than a filename; images no longer offer a generic Translate action. Descriptions as well as text. Image reading starts with a short visual description, even for photos without words. Screenshots retain structured useful content and documents keep faithful transcription. AI text into your caption, by choice. Beside Copy, Add to caption accepts a result without touching the original body or media. An existing caption asks before appending; concurrent edits are preserved. One clean writing surface. Capture and every Android multiline editor use the surrounding field's fill again; the separate grey rectangle introduced in 2.0.3 is removed, including unfilled and translucent fields. Lighter Android editing. Editors use texture composition again instead of forcing the whole scene through hybrid composition. The Android host uses TextureView so the system magnifier can sample the text and its background together; selection, formatting and keyboard behaviour are preserved.

item.title: Nex 2.0.3
item.description: Consistent glass borders. The settings search field, profile card, birthday row and home-widget settings panels use the shared glass surface and edge. Clearer floating glass. Card menus, popup menus and the home navigation/selection bars reveal more of the blurred page beneath them, with readable ink and opaque high-contrast fallbacks. Save selected text to Nex. Android's text-selection menu offers Save to Nex in compatible apps. It uses quick capture, leaves the source text unchanged and returns to the app you were using. Cleaner text selection. Android's editor uses native composition and a readable magnifier background instead of an empty floating lens. A compact module catalog. Search names and descriptions; tap a card to reveal full details and Add, Open or Remove actions. Browsing leaves modules off. Edit attached images. Hold an image attached to a note and choose Edit to crop or annotate it. Saving preserves its position and caption, keeps the original file safe and refreshes image text. Useful image reading. AI turns screenshots into organized reports focused on the main content, skipping keyboard keys and routine interface clutter. Documents and receipts keep faithful transcription; unclear details are never guessed.

item.title: Nex 2.0.2
item.description: Small, visible swipe feedback. Standard icons give one brief pulse when revealed and when a full swipe arms. The motion finishes while your finger pauses and stays still with reduced motion. Glass reaches the assistant and modules. The chat sheet no longer covers glass with an opaque layer; assistant settings, composer, module headers, dialogs and menus share the same material. A fine rim reflection adds depth, with solid high-contrast fallbacks. Modules start off. All modules are available in Tools → Add modules and are off until you add them. The automatic 2.0.1 preview no longer enables them; explicit Add/Remove choices are preserved. Bold keeps your line breaks. Formatting part of a note no longer pulls the next line up beside it; typed Enter stays a new line. The + button follows the shortcut colour. Its fill gradually takes the selected capture type's colour as you swipe and returns when you cancel. Faster editing scroll. A quick vertical flick in Android's editor continues with bounded momentum. Touching again stops it, while long-press selection and handles keep their normal behaviour.

item.title: Nex 2.0.1
item.description: Eleven modules to try. Habits, Price Lens, Lent & Borrowed, Expenses, Gold, Words, Parking, Medicine, Warranty, Maintenance and Smoke Free are available and already added in Tools for this preview. Remove or re-add each independently. Their data stays local and in backups, separate from notes, search and the assistant; camera, GPS, network and background reminders remain future integrations. Glass across the app. Page headers, confirmation dialogs, popup and note-action menus, Settings groups and Tools/Library panels now share the optional frosted material. High contrast stays opaque and note cards keep their reading surface. Ready-made swipe motion. Replaced the hand-drawn swipe glyphs with bundled useAnimations and Animate UI assets. Motion follows the swipe and reverses as you pull back, works offline and respects reduced motion.

item.title: Nex 2.0.0
item.description: Paste without a keyboard blink. The capture editor keeps its active focus when pasting in Note, Checklist and Link. Photos arrive straight away. Camera and gallery captures save directly by default. Turn on “Edit photos before capture” in Settings → Capture to open the preview first; existing photos remain editable from their detail page. Swipe icons tell their own story. The bin lid opens, the tag unfolds, the pin presses down, the bell clapper swings, the share arrow rises and the assistant's stars light up as you swipe. Pull back to reverse the gesture; the action thresholds stay the same. Reduced motion keeps the icons still. Liquid glass returns as an optional material. Enable it in Settings → Appearance. Floating controls and sheets gain frosted depth and a fine optical rim while notes stay solid and readable. Off by default, independent of your theme, with opaque surfaces in high contrast. Widgets refresh their colours completely. Old custom tints no longer linger after restoring default colours; the logo keeps its own light/dark colours and custom action colours stay legible. Two finishing touches. The birthday countdown follows light/dark correctly in Nex and Graphite. Library and Settings now give the same optional haptic tick as the other home-dock destinations.

item.title: Nex 1.99.99
item.description: Sponsor cards in both interfaces. Campaigns prefer the interface language; when none matches, an available campaign still appears in Persian or English. Switching languages no longer hides the cached card. Repeating reminders show their clock. A repeat icon and “Daily · 09:00” replace “Every day”; weekly reminders name the weekday and time. Hold the label for the full schedule, also available to screen readers. Tap away to stop selecting. Tapping outside a note or caption clears the text selection and its menu, including notes with links. Copy, selection handles and link gestures keep working. Sponsor cards recover more reliably. A temporary picture error keeps a usable cached picture; missing pictures retry after the shorter cool-off. Unreadable pictures show the campaign’s words, and network reads stay within their time and size limits. Paste, inside the capture box. A small clipboard icon in the editor's corner works for Note, Checklist and Link. It pastes at the caret or replaces selected words, keeping the rest of your text. Card indicators stay together. Reminders and attached-file counts sit on a compact, consistent row below the preview, independent of the note's language. Both preview lines keep their full width; cards without indicators stay compact.

item.title: Nex 1.99.98
item.description: A cleaner capture box. One outline around the editor; Note, Checklist and Link stay together above it. Voice joins Camera, Gallery and File below, each directly reachable in its own type colour. Swiping + has its own light. A border in the shortcut’s Settings colour traces the screen as your finger moves, completes before the shortcut opens, and retracts if you cancel. Left and right keep your chosen actions in every theme and language. A deliberate hold for the assistant. A short pause before its glow starts keeps taps and sideways swipes from flashing the assistant. Holding still continues to open it; reduced motion skips the light. The keyboard leaves with the editor. After adding a link to selected words, saving or leaving the note editor or capture box no longer leaves the keyboard behind. Saving or cancelling the link returns to the original field; all other text formats keep working. Links work as soon as you write them. Web addresses in ordinary notes and captions are recognised without adding another formatted link first. Tap a link to open it in your browser; hold it for Open link and Copy link. Ordinary words still select and copy as before.

item.title: Nex 1.99.97
item.description: One capture box for everything. Note, voice, checklist and link now sit at the top of the box and switch in place — what you typed stays, so a note becomes a list without typing it again, and a pasted address becomes a link (a line around it becomes its caption). Record right in the box. Voice turns the box itself into a recorder with a live waveform; stop keeps it, the bin throws it away and brings your words back. A shorter row of tools. The camera keeps its own button; the gallery and files share one clip menu. Flick + for a shortcut. Flick the + button left or right to start a voice note or the camera straight away — choose both in Settings → Gestures.

item.title: Nex 1.99.96
item.description: Ask the assistant about Nex itself. "How do I pin a tool?", "why did my reminder not ring?", "how do I move to a new phone?" — it now answers from the app's own guide, in your language, and says where in the app to go. A fuller guide. The guide now explains the app lock in detail, lists what each settings page holds, and answers the common questions. The app lock is harder to loosen. Making Nex lock later — or only when you ask — now asks for your fingerprint first, so nobody holding your phone for a moment can change it. Locking sooner still takes one tap. Locking closes everything. When Nex locks, the private tools lock with it and the keyboard closes, so nothing typed at the lock lands in a hidden note. The lock says what is wrong. After too many wrong fingerprints it tells you to wait or to unlock the phone first, and if the phone has no screen lock it offers to open the phone's settings to set one. A better photo editor. A photo the camera saved on its side now opens the right way up for cropping, and comes out that way. Crop pills, round tools and a new Flip ; in drawing, a tap leaves a dot, lines are smoother, the slider also sets the size of text, a label can be held to change or remove it, Redo joins Undo, and text sits where you tapped. The editor is dark in every theme, so none of its buttons fade into the background, and turning and cropping a camera photo is quicker and no longer makes a much larger file along the way.

item.title: Nex 1.99.95
item.description: Reminders and attachments cost a card no line. They sit at the end of the note's last line, the way a message's time does in a chat: a short note keeps them on its one line, and a long one fades out just before them. Its words keep every line they had. A folded smart summary stays folded. It used to open again on its own when you came back to the app, as if it were opening to update; now it updates inside the folded card, and only a tap opens it. The lock on private tools opens with them. On the Tools page and on tools pinned to the home screen, the lock shows open while Passwords, Bank cards and Private messages are unlocked, and closes again when they lock. A voice note whose file will not open now says so under the player instead of leaving its button dimmed, and a recording that wrote nothing is no longer saved as an empty note.

item.title: Nex 1.99.94
item.description: Voice notes open again. In 1.99.93 opening a voice note or an audio file froze the app and left a grey box where the player should be. It opens and plays again. Reminders and attachments fit on every card. The line under the note's words takes the place of its last line, so on a compact card it is no longer cut off at the bottom, and it sits on the same side as the words — on the right under a Persian note. A voice note's length joins it on that line.

item.title: Nex 1.99.93
item.description: A new player for recordings. Voice notes, audio files and attached voice clips play in one new player: a round button that turns play into pause and glows while it plays, the recording's own shape as the bar — touch or drag it to move — and a speed button for 1×, 1.5× and 2×. It is there the moment the note opens, instead of appearing a second later. Voice notes are recorded the way voice clips are. On some phones a voice note recorded with + still played nothing, while a clip attached on the same phone played. A voice note is now recorded exactly like that clip. Search, as it should be. With nothing typed, a touch outside the search box leaves search. With words typed and the keyboard up, the first touch anywhere — a result included — only closes the keyboard; then a result opens with a tap, and the keyboard no longer comes back when you close it. Reminders and attachments under the words. On a card they now sit on a small line beneath the note instead of in a column beside it, so the note's words get the card's whole width. The filter and clear buttons sit in the middle of the search box.

item.title: Nex 1.99.92
item.description: Voice notes play on every phone. On some phones a voice note recorded with + played nothing, while a clip attached on the same phone played: the recording was labelled with the sample rate and channels that were asked for, not the ones the phone used. Each recording now carries the phone's own, and voice notes recorded before play from a corrected copy — the original stays as it is. Attaching no longer holds everything else up. With reading text in photos or transcription on, each attached photo or voice clip made the app wait for the AI before doing anything else — a file attached or a note deleted could take minutes to appear. It is read in the background now, the way a photo note's own text always was. Tools on the home screen. Hold any tool on the Tools page — passwords, bank cards, scheduled notes, the generator, a module — to pin it to the top of the timeline, in its own colour and icon. A pinned private tool shows only its name and still asks for your fingerprint. Hold it there to take it off. Recent searches. Before you type, your last five searches are there to tap again, next to the saved ones, with a button to clear them. A finished checklist says so. Ticking the last open line makes the list glow once, the phone gives a single tap, and the progress line reads All done . Touch the Nex wordmark on the home screen and it plays its little movement there and then.

item.title: Nex 1.99.91
item.description: Meaning search speaks again. Since 1.99.82 it could find nothing at all. When no note stands out for a search, the few notes plainly close to it are shown again — still only those, and still after the notes with your words. Search waits for the keyboard. While you type in the search, the first touch outside the field only closes the keyboard — it no longer opens a result or closes the search by accident. Then a result opens with a tap, the field brings the keyboard back, and a touch anywhere else leaves the search. Save to device works for every item again. A photo — a note's own or an attached one — and a note of words (saved as Markdown) said "Couldn't save"; they now go wherever you choose, as files and recordings already did. Voice notes play. A voice note just recorded could play nothing at all: its first moment was the recorder's setup, written as if it were sound. New recordings start with the sound itself. At the end of a recording the button turns back to Play and the next tap starts from the beginning. The progress bar stays put. Playing a voice note or an attached recording, the bar no longer runs ahead for a moment and snaps back to the start. Holding an attachment. The held tile settles back into its place before its menu opens, instead of passing over the menu. Nex's diagnostics can be shared to Nex. Sending the diagnostics file from About to Nex itself makes a note of it, instead of a warning. A photo whose file is missing shows as missing in the viewer, instead of being logged as an error.

item.title: Nex 1.99.90
item.description: Attachments, grown up. Photos open in one gallery with every photo of the note — swipe between them, with each caption at the bottom and where you are at the top. Tiles show what each file is: a PDF by its first page, a video by a frame, a voice clip by its length, any other file by its kind and extension, and a photo's caption along its bottom. The Attached row says how many files there are and how much room they take. Voice clips on notes. Attach → Record a voice clip adds a spoken note to a photo of a receipt or a whiteboard. Tap it to play it in place; with transcription on, what is said is found by search. More from a hold. Hold an attachment and let go for its menu: share it or save it to your device on its own, rename a file, make an attached photo the note's own photo, or take it out as a note of its own. The reminder and the paperclip together. On a card, the reminder and the count of attached files now sit together at the end, one above the other, instead of at opposite ends of the note's words.

item.title: Nex 1.99.81
item.description: Search keeps what you typed on top. Notes that contain your words now always come first, in the order they first appear, and no longer move when the search by meaning answers a moment later. Notes found only by meaning follow them — only the few closest, marked as before. Before, a note that merely resembled the query could sit above the notes that held the words, and a long tail of unrelated notes was listed as found by meaning. Search by meaning, stricter. It now keeps only matches close to its best one, and the on-device search model needs a closer match than before, so a query with nothing related in your notes is no longer answered with unrelated ones. Opening search, visible. The field now lights up with a soft glow in your accent colour, and the results rise into place one after another.

item.title: Nex 1.99.80
item.description: Share several files into Nex at once. Choose several photos or files in your gallery or file manager and share them to Nex: they become one note — the first is the note, the rest are attached to it. Before, Nex was not even offered for more than one file. Drag attachments into order. Hold an attachment on a note and drag it; hold it and let go for its menu, which can now also move it earlier or later. Words in attached photos are searchable. With reading text in photos on, the photos attached to a note are read like a photo note's own, so a serial number on the third photo finds the note. Details that tell you something. More → Details now says how long ago a note was made and last changed (or that it never was), how many words it has, how much of a checklist is ticked, a recording's length, a link's site, and how much room the note takes with its attachments. It closes with Close , not Cancel. The profile's sky works. The constellation behind your name was drawn into a single dot. It now fills the card: a star for each letter of your name, drifting and twinkling, with a spark now and then running along its lines. The floating date, calmer. The date that appears as you scroll the timeline now drops in from under the filters and tucks back, rolls to the next day in the direction you are scrolling, and has no shadow. Search opens and closes smoothly. The field, its buttons and the results now ease in and out together instead of switching on a frame. A form just for module ideas. The row at the foot of the Modules page opens a short form for your idea, without the bug and diagnostics options of the general feedback form — and its arrow points the right way in Persian.

item.title: Nex 1.99.60
item.description: Modules: add only what you need. Extra features now live in Tools → Modules , each on a card that says what it does. One that is not added takes no room and runs nothing — no tile, no reminders, no widgets, no assistant tools — and removing one asks whether to keep its data or delete it. More modules will arrive this way, so Nex stays light for everyone who does not want them. Cycle is the first module. It moved from your profile to Tools → Modules. If you already use it, it stays on, with all its data; it now appears in Tools under Modules. Note colours that match your theme. The colour of each item's icon (lists, links, voice, photos, files) used to be fixed: a mustard link on a blue theme. Now every type takes a shade of your own accent, fanned out around it on the colour wheel. Each theme gets its own family of colours, and every icon stays easy to read against its square. What is coming to Modules. Tools → Modules now lists what is on the way, each marked Soon or Planned: Smoke-free, Where I parked, Gold check, Word by word, Telegram bridge, Medicine cabinet, Warranties, Lent & borrowed and Habits. A row at the bottom sends your own idea for a module straight to us. Adding a module feels like installing it. Tap Add and you watch it go in: small pieces in the module's colour gather into its icon while a ring closes around it, with each step and the percentage below. When the ring meets itself a check pops on, and the card moves up to the modules you have added. Removing one runs it backwards, then tells you it is gone. With animations turned off it happens at once. One way of moving, everywhere. Sheets, dialogs, pages and cards now arrive and leave in the same rhythm: they arrive softly, and leave a little quicker than they came. Dialogs used to fade in at a different speed from the sheets they opened over, and some sheets slid while others rose. Now everything moves alike.

item.title: Nex 1.99.50
item.description: Notes open faster. A note's sheet now opens with the note already in it — it used to rise with a placeholder and wait for the library before growing to fit — and it rises in about a third less time. A clearer top to every note. The sheet opens on its type in the colour its card wears, and the date with the month in words and the time to the minute; the exact time to the second is still under Details. Days fold like a fan. Folding a day — by tapping its heading or pinching the timeline — now moves its notes one after another: opening, they fan out from the heading and settle into place; closing, the lowest go first and the rest fold up after them. The wordmark takes your accent, and comes alive. The stroke through the x and the dot after it in the corner of the timeline now wear the app's accent colour instead of a fixed blue — green with Forest, and so on — and every few seconds a light runs along the stroke and the dot gives a small hop. Never with animations turned off.

item.title: Nex 1.99.40
item.description: A first run that shows instead of tells. The welcome pages are new: the octopus catches the pieces of a day as they drift in, notes land on a small timeline with nothing to save, a search finds «کتاب» even when it is typed with Arabic letters, and a lock closes round all of it. Each picture plays once and holds still while you read. Six pages became four, with a bar showing how far along you are. Your greeting, before you start. The last welcome page draws the top of the timeline live: type your name and Nex greets you by it, in the theme and language you are picking, so you can see what each answer changes. Each kind of note has its colour. On every card the square beside the note takes its type's colour — text in your theme's accent, voice violet, checklists teal, links amber, photos rose, files grey — so a day's voice notes and lists stand out at a glance. The empty timeline's three ways in wear the same colours. A day reads as one strand. The notes under each date are joined by a thin thread down their squares, and the date headings are bolder and easier to scan. A lighter top of the timeline. Today's date — in your calendar, with the month in words — sits over the greeting, now set at the start of the line; the filter button moved beside the search field, and the row of tag chips appears only once there are tags to pick, so the first notes start well up the screen. Appearance and Security, chosen in place. Theme, text size and card size are now the choices themselves on the Theme page — card size drawn as stacks of cards — instead of rows that each opened a sheet. Security opens on whether Nex asks before it opens, and when to lock is three choices with a line each, plus the delay as chips. A clearer password generator. The password sits on its own card with a meter for how strong it is, and copy and a fresh one side by side.

item.title: Nex 1.99.30
item.description: Sharing no longer says "could not be stored" over a share that was saved. An older share whose file could no longer be read stayed waiting in Nex and was tried again under every new share, so each one reported a failure while its note was already in the timeline. Only the share you just made is reported now, and one that keeps failing is let go after a few tries. The assistant's light leaves the way it came. When the assistant closes, its border no longer vanishes at once: the ring of light runs back down both sides of the screen to the + button and goes out there in a soft pulse. Language & calendar, at a glance. The calendar choice shows today's date on a little calendar leaf in each calendar, a preview card shows how a day heading and a note will look with your language and calendar, and the language AI answers in can be set here as well. Intelligence, redesigned. Its page opens on whether it is on, with whom, and how many abilities are working; the six abilities are tiles you switch with one tap, greyed with the reason when your provider cannot do them; and "What left this device" sits next to the provider. The Intelligence category shows the same at a glance. Tools, on two shelves. The private tools (passwords, bank cards, private messages) sit together under a lock, and Cycle, Scheduled and the password generator under Everyday; each tool has its own colour, so it is found at a glance. Library and its lists, in the new look. The Library opens on three coloured shelves — Tags, Threads and Trash — each saying how much it holds, above the storage card; the lists of tags, threads, deleted notes and requests that left the device are drawn as rounded cards, each tag on a tile in its own colour; Recurring's three counts each have their own colour; Speed and reliability sits on cards. Tidier settings pages. Home screen widget and About Nex are grouped into cards like the rest of Settings. Fixes. "Persian" is shown in Persian letters on the language cards, longer choice names wrap instead of being cut off, and a photo whose file has gone no longer logs an error. Receipts stay with their Recurring item. A receipt photo added to a Recurring item no longer appears among your notes on the home screen, and deleting a note no longer takes a receipt off its item: receipts are the item's own, shown as thumbnails you tap to see full screen. Ones added before this update are still linked notes. A colour you pick shows as that colour. On every palette but Nex, a chosen accent was muted to fit the palette — a red came out brown — and on Graphite it was ignored altogether. It now keeps its own colour, and on Graphite it is the one colour among the greys.

item.title: Nex 1.99.20
item.description: Settings is a page. It opens like Tools and the Library instead of rising from the bottom, so a pull at its top can no longer close it by accident; the search box at its top now has the same rounded shape as everything under it. A new Profile page. Your picture sits on a coloured header with a small constellation drawn from your name — every name draws its own — and the name and bio show there as you type them. Tap the picture to choose one from the gallery, take one with Nex's camera, or remove it: removing it is no longer a wide button under the picture that a tap beside it could hit. The birthday shows your age and counts the days to the next one, by the Persian calendar when you use it, and the bio's label sits where it belongs. Gestures and menus in one tap. Every swipe action is now a chip under its edge, and a small card shows what each swipe will uncover in its own colour; the hold menu's actions are switched on and off on the same page, without opening another one. App icons: dark above, light below. The blue octopus is gone and the swirl now also comes on light, so each of the three icons has a dark and a light version in the same column; the previews are a little smaller. Every theme has its own motif, higher up. Autumn now has falling leaves, Rose atelier blossoms, Saffron threads of saffron and Graphite graph paper, and Midnight gains a crescent moon among its stars; only the plain Nex look stays plain. The motifs now rise over the lower half of the screen instead of the bottom third. Themes you can see before you choose. The palettes on the Theme page are now a gallery of small previews, each in its own page colour with a note card in its tones and its motif, and the settings above them sit on a card like the rest of Settings.

item.title: Nex 1.99.10
item.description: Speaking to the assistant happens in the message bar. The microphone no longer opens the voice-note sheet over the assistant: the message bar itself becomes the recording, with the conversation still in view — ✕ cancels, the time and your voice as it is heard in the middle, ↑ sends. The microphone and send share one button: the microphone while the box is empty. Backup & restore, simpler. The page (formerly "Taking it with you") now starts with whether you are backed up and one Back up now ; then what happens automatically, the restore points on this phone (tap one to restore, share or delete it), and three plain choices: a complete backup, an export of your notes, and one Restore or import from a file for every kind of file. Automatic backups no longer wait for a restart. They ran only when Nex was started from scratch, and Android often keeps it running in the background for days — so a day could pass with no backup. They now also run whenever you come back to Nex. The daily folder copy no longer adds a second restore point on the phone, which pushed older ones out. Private saved messages, redesigned. Messages have room between them, are grouped by day and show their time, and the box and its buttons no longer touch. A photo opens full screen with zoom, as on the home screen; a file opens with a tap or goes to another app with its share icon; a voice message shows how far it has played. Tap a message for copy, open, share or delete. Everything about a bank card, on the card. The number, name, CVV2 and expiry on its face, and the IBAN, account number, bank and notes beneath it on the same card — each copied with a tap, nothing listed twice. Nex's own camera in more places. A receipt for a Recurring item and a photo in Private saved messages are now taken with the same camera panel as a photo note — and in private messages the photo goes straight into the vault, never into your notes. No sponsor card in your first days. A new install sees none until it is ten days old or holds five notes, whichever comes first. Cycle: a ring you can touch. Touch the ring to see any day of the cycle — its date, its day and its stage — and the middle to come back to today. Today's stage (period, follicular, fertile window or luteal) is named under the ring. Cycle: a word for today and one-tap mood. A short, gentle tip for where you are in the cycle, different each day, and a row of faces to log your mood without opening the day. Cycle asks when a period seems forgotten. A period left open longer than yours usually last brings a gentle "Has it ended?" instead of the page going on with "period, day 12". Cycle fixes. A period can now be ended in Breastfeeding and Menopause modes, where only "Period started" appeared; a late period no longer leaves predicted days in the past on the calendar; and a month you forgot to log is no longer flagged as a long cycle.

item.title: Nex 1.99.9
item.description: Talk to the assistant. With Gemini or OpenAI as your provider, the microphone in the assistant now sends what you say as your message, so you can ask and get things done by voice; anything it would change still waits for your confirmation. To see the words first, turn on Check what I said before sending in the assistant's settings. Voice, photos and files in private messages. The + beside the box in Private saved messages attaches a voice message, a photo or a file, with what you typed as its caption. Attachments are encrypted on this phone and are not part of backups. The smart summary sees your reminders. A reminder set more than a week ahead was invisible to it, so it could advise setting a reminder you had already set. It now knows about every reminder. The assistant knows more about your notes. Every note it reads now says whether it is pinned, its reminder if it has one, the thread it is in, and the day it was written, so it no longer offers a reminder or a pin that is already there and can answer "what did I write last week". It can also look at your tags, your recurring items with when each is next due, and Recently Deleted, so "when is the insurance due?" and "bring back the note I deleted" work, and it knows your current settings before changing one. Ticking a checklist item by voice or chat now ticks the right one. A link is kept when you close its sheet, as text and checklists are, as long as it is a complete address. The assistant asks before reading a tag or a thread you did not mention. It already asked before searching for words you had not used; a note could otherwise point it at a whole tag of notes to send to the provider. A Cycle summary read on the phone stays on the phone. If a conversation the phone's model had about your cycle is continued with a cloud provider, that summary is no longer sent along; the provider gets Cycle only by asking for it, with your permission, as before.

item.title: Nex 1.99.8
item.description: A recording survives the app closing. If Nex was closed in the middle of a voice memo — the phone ran short of memory, or the app crashed — the recording was lost, and the file left behind could not even be played. Recordings are now saved as they are made, and the next time you open Nex the interrupted one appears as a voice note, up to the moment it stopped. Search by meaning on the phone shows real matches only. With the on-device search model, a search could list every note as "Found by meaning", even ones about something else entirely. That model now has a cut-off of its own, so unrelated notes stay out. What's new is in Persian too. With the app in Persian, the update screen shows the release notes in Persian. Scrolling far back stays fast. Each page of older notes used to reload every note above it, so a long scroll got slower the further it went. New pages are now added to the end. A quicker start for heavy assistant users. Saved conversations moved out of the app's settings into a file of their own, read only when you open the assistant; they still go into settings backups. A note being typed is not wound back. In a rare case, reopening the app could restore an older copy of a note you were typing over a newer one already saved. The newer one is now kept. Opening a library from a newer Nex. If an older version of Nex is installed over a newer one, it now says the library needs the newer version, instead of offering to restore a backup over it. Under the hood. The on-device assistant counts code and symbols more carefully, so a library of code notes no longer overflows it; the build without on-device models no longer carries their 22 MB runtime; release builds report whether native libraries suit phones with 16 KB memory pages; a test opens a library from the first release and checks that nothing is lost.

item.title: Nex 1.99.7
item.description: Cycle stays private when the app locks. A home-screen Cycle widget that was refreshing at the moment the app lock closed could show your dates again afterwards. It now always ends on the locked state. Deleting Cycle really deletes it from this phone. The backups on the phone still held every period and logged day. They are now replaced with one that does not, and the confirmation says plainly that copies you saved elsewhere are not changed. No leftover copies of imported files. Importing a password CSV or restoring a backup left a full, unencrypted copy of the file in the app's cache. The copy is now deleted as soon as it has been read, and any old ones are cleared when the app starts. Updates from Cafe Bazaar and Myket. If you installed Nex from Cafe Bazaar or Myket, the app no longer looks for updates on its own; the update screen tells you they come from the store. Copies installed another way keep updating in the app. A privacy policy in the app. Under About Nex → Privacy policy, in Persian and English: what stays on the phone, when anything leaves it, and what you control. The guide's privacy paragraph now also mentions link previews and model downloads. TalkBack can read and copy the recovery code, and the Cycle calendar says what each day is (period, expected, fertile, likely ovulation, logged) and opens it. The recurring-items calendar's days open with TalkBack too. Cycle periods can no longer overlap. Editing a period onto another's dates is refused with a message, instead of quietly skewing every prediction. Search by meaning follows your edits. An edited note used to be found by what it said before; it is now prepared again in the background after each change. The on-device smart summary no longer spins forever. A summary the phone's model never finishes is given up on after two minutes. No raw instructions in the chat. When the assistant wrote an action without its usual wrapping, the chat showed it as code above the confirmation card. It now shows only the card. Sharing a video no longer says it failed. A video shared from Telegram, WhatsApp or the gallery was saved, but the message said "Capture could not be stored". A share that is in your notes is now always reported as saved. Words under a shared video or photo come with it. When Telegram, WhatsApp or another app sends text along with a file, it becomes the note's caption. The assistant knows which checklist items are done. It used to read ticked items as still to do; it now sees what is left and what is already done. More actions closes with a swipe down, like every other sheet. Gemma 4's licence is Apache 2.0. The on-device model page now shows that licence and links to it, instead of the older Gemma terms. More from the same review, smaller but real: Deleting all assistant conversations now asks first, and an assistant change that fails part-way says how many changes were made instead of only "That didn't work". A note shared into Nex from another app can be found by meaning right away, not only after the next launch; a very long note no longer stops the others from being prepared for search; and asking the phone's model about one note lets it read the whole note. The on-device assistant no longer gets a line telling it to answer general questions when "Stay in my notes" is on. The Cycle calendar marks the likely ovulation day with its own ring and legend; the ring's text fits at the largest text sizes; and a few Persian phrases are corrected. Persian users get the solar calendar by default until they choose otherwise. An export now carries notes scheduled for later, and importing an export is all-or-nothing, so a retry never duplicates notes. The download notification shows its percentage in Persian digits, and a long model download pauses cleanly when Android 15's daily limit for background transfers is reached. A backup that would unpack to far more than its own size is refused; file previews and "Save to device" only open the app's own files; the search model is only loaded from where Nex installed it; and the app no longer asks for access to your photos, videos and audio, which it never used. The licences page now lists the on-device model runtime. Android's notification settings name Nex's channels (Reminders, Daily digest, Updates) in the app's language. "OCR" is now "Text in the photo", and the empty search says "Start typing to find a note".

item.title: Nex 1.99.6
item.description: The on-device assistant answers questions about your period. Asked "how many days until my period?", the model on your phone guessed a number or said it could not see Cycle, because it is meant to ask for your Cycle summary first and seldom did. Now, when you ask about your period, cycle, ovulation or pregnancy and the assistant is allowed to read Cycle, Nex reads the summary for it before it answers, and you see "Read your Cycle summary" as you do with a cloud provider. Nothing leaves your phone for this. Fewer raw instructions in the chat. When the on-device model wrote a request to look something up in a slightly wrong shape, the chat showed it as code instead of carrying it out. Those shapes are now understood.

item.title: Nex 1.99.5
item.description: The on-device assistant answers with many notes and long conversations. The phone's model reads about 4,000 tokens at a time — the assistant's instructions, your notes and the conversation together — and once a library or a chat grew past that, every message was refused and the chat said the model would not start. Requests are now fitted to it: the notes found for your question come first, each note line is kept short, older turns of a long conversation give way to the newest, and the action instructions take a shorter form when room is tight. Your newest question is always kept. The smart summary is written in the language you chose. With the summary language set to Persian, the on-device model could still answer in English, even repeating labels like "DUE" from what it was given. The language is now the first thing it is told and the last, and those labels are no longer copied into the summary. Clearer expectations for each assistant. The on-device model page now says plainly that a model on the phone does not reach the quality of a cloud model, and the cloud provider page that how good the results are depends entirely on the model you choose.

item.title: Nex 1.99.4
item.description: The on-device assistant starts reliably. Opening the assistant and sending a message at the same moment loaded the model twice, which does not fit in a phone's memory, and the app could close mid-load. After that, the model could refuse to start for good, showing "would not start on this phone" on every message. Now it loads once whoever asks, a load that was cut short is simply tried again, and the on-device model page has Try loading it again , so you never have to download it again to recover. When it still will not start, the chat shows the runtime's own message under the error. MiniCPM5 is no longer offered. It closed the app on the phones it was tried on, so Gemma 4 E2B is the on-device model again. If you had MiniCPM installed, its 1.45 GB is freed the next time you open the on-device model page.

item.title: Nex 1.99.3
item.description: Search by meaning, right on your phone. A new on-device search model, EmbeddingGemma 2 (about 160 MB), is in Settings → Intelligence → On-device search . Once downloaded, Nex finds notes by what they mean with no internet and no AI provider: in search, in related notes, and when the assistant looks for the notes that answer your question — so the on-device assistant finds the right note even when you ask in different words. Nothing you write is sent anywhere for it. It only finds; it does not chat, so it sits beside the assistant's models rather than among them. Your notes are prepared for it in the background after it is installed.

item.title: Nex 1.99.2
item.description: The smart summary reads what you just wrote. Reminders and open lists used to take every line, so a note from this morning without a reminder never made it in. A share of the summary is now kept for the last two days' notes: it says where you left off, and when a note mentions a day or time — "tomorrow", "on the 14th" — with no reminder set, it suggests one. Your tags are read too, so related things are said together ("three things left for the trip"), and a note that is only a record, like a saved link or a receipt, is not mentioned on its own. "Full" in the smart summary is really fuller. It was held to the same four short lines as "Standard", so choosing it changed nothing. Now "Brief" is two short lines, "Standard" four, and "Full" up to eight, each with room to say why it matters or what to do next. A quiet day is still short under all three. The assistant sees Cycle as soon as you allow it. After turning on "Let the assistant read Cycle", an open chat still said it could not see Cycle until you started a new one. It now goes by the setting as it is when you ask, and turning the setting off stops what it read earlier from being sent again.

item.title: Nex 1.99.1
item.description: MiniCPM5 installs now. In 1.99.0 its download finished and then the model was removed by mistake, so it never became active. Download it again from the on-device model page. Nothing from the failed attempts is left on your phone: leftover and half-finished files are cleared, and the page shows how much of an unfinished download is already there. On-device model downloads keep going in the background. Like an app update, the download shows its progress in the notification shade and continues when you leave Nex; Back on the home screen sends Nex to the background instead of stopping it. The on-device assistant knows it is Nex's assistant. It now sees its instructions and your notes on every model, so it answers about your notes instead of introducing itself as the bare model. What the assistant looks up is no longer shown as your message. When it reads your Cycle summary or searches your notes, a small line says so — "Read your Cycle summary", "Searched your notes" — instead of a bubble of raw data in your name. Pull to refresh always refreshes the smart summary. A pull made while a summary was already being written used to do nothing; it now waits for that one, and asks again if it brought nothing new. With the length limit lifted, a summary that never comes back no longer blocks the card. The sponsor card recovers after a wrong phone date. A phone whose date was once set in the future no longer holds the card back until that date comes round.

item.title: Nex 1.99.0
item.description: Cycle is now turned on in your profile, and off by default. A card in Profile says in a few lines what Cycle does, with the switch to turn it on and a way straight in. If you were already using Cycle, it stays on. The old switch in Settings → Sections is gone; searching Settings for "Cycle" points to your profile. Every sheet closes with a swipe down. Pulling a sheet's content down from the top now closes it, not only its handle — Cycle's settings and day log included, which could not be swiped away before. A second on-device model to try. In the on-device model page you can now choose between Gemma 4 E2B and the lighter MiniCPM5 2B (1.45 GB). Each downloads separately, and the one you pick is the one the assistant uses — no restart needed. A full backup includes the model in use. Two Cycle widgets. Cycle shows the ring, where you are in your cycle, the fertile window and a kind word for the day, in Cycle's own soft colours. Cycle, discreet is just the ring and one number, with no words. Both stay right day by day without opening Nex, open Cycle when tapped, and show nothing while the app lock is closed.

item.title: Nex 1.98.0
item.description: Cycle has a space of its own. The page now feels like stepping into a quieter room: a soft blush-to-lavender light whose glows drift gently as you scroll, rounded frosted cards, a glowing ring and a rose button. It opens with a greeting for the time of day and a kind line for where you are in your cycle — "Be gentle with yourself today" during a period. Its sheets and dialogs share the same colours. With reduced motion, nothing moves. Fertility signs when trying to conceive. In Trying to conceive mode, a day's log also takes your temperature on waking, an ovulation test and cervical mucus. A positive test is shown on the page for the rest of that cycle, and the assistant (only if you allowed it to read Cycle) sees these signs too. Gentle companion. A new switch in Cycle's settings, off by default. When it is on, on the days that are often harder — the few days before a period, its first days, or a day you logged feeling low, sensitive or in pain — the assistant answers more softly and patiently, like a caring friend. It never brings up your cycle or suggests a reason for how you feel. Only a line about tone is sent to your AI provider, never your cycle data. After the due date, Cycle asks. In Pregnant mode, once the due date has passed Cycle asks whether your baby has arrived and offers to switch to Breastfeeding or back to Normal in one tap.

item.title: Nex 1.96.0
item.description: Cycle — a menstrual cycle assistant. A new Cycle page in Tools . Three optional questions to begin; then one large button for "Period started" and "Period ended", a ring showing where you are in your cycle, and a month calendar (in the solar calendar when you use it) with your periods, the expected ones and the likely fertile days. Predictions from your own history , not a fixed 28 days: a range rather than a single date, and a plain note of how sure it is. A month you forgot to log is not mistaken for one long cycle. A day's log in a few taps: flow, mood, energy, symptoms, pain relief, intimacy, the pill and a short note. Your averages and past periods , each period editable or deletable. A gentle word, never a diagnosis, when something is unusual: a period much later than expected, one lasting more than eight days, very short or long cycles, or cycles that vary a lot. Optional reminders two days before a period, each evening of a period, and for a daily pill. They only ever say "Nex reminder". Private by design: kept only on this phone and in your backups, never in your notes, search or widgets, and never sent to an AI service. Delete all cycle data removes everything at once. Cycle is not a method of contraception and does not replace a doctor.

item.title: Nex 1.95.0
item.description: Schedule a note for later. While writing a note, hold the send button instead of tapping it, and choose when it should arrive: tomorrow morning, next week, in a month, in a year, or any day and time. Until then it is nowhere in your notes, search or widgets; at its time it lands on the timeline as an ordinary note, with a notification. Tools → Scheduled lists what is on its way, where each one can be delivered now, moved to another time or discarded. Compact cards sit closer together. With Card size → Compact , the cards on the timeline are spaced more tightly, so a screen holds more of them. The other two sizes are unchanged. Picking notes feels like one bar turning into another. When you start selecting notes, the bottom bar narrows and sinks away while the selection bar rises in its place and its buttons appear one after another. With reduced motion, the bars simply swap.

item.title: Nex 1.93.5
item.description: A diagnostics report that keeps what matters. The report on your phone now keeps up to 100 errors and 50 other app events, apart, so routine events can no longer push real errors out. An event that repeats is recorded once, with how many times and since when. It used to keep only 20 entries in all, and a reminder rescheduled on every launch could fill them by itself. Attach the report to feedback. When you send feedback you can tick Attach the diagnostics report . The exact report is shown before sending, with links, keys and passwords removed and nothing from your notes. It is never sent unless you tick it.

item.title: Nex 1.93.4
item.description: Password import no longer fails on one bad row. Importing from Chrome or Google Password Manager now brings in every row it can read and lists the ones it could not, by line and with the reason. A row with no password, which Google exports for passkeys and "never save" sites, no longer stops the whole file. Passwords with Persian letters, numbers a spreadsheet saved as formulas, semicolon-separated files and files saved again in Windows-1256 all import, and the private section now holds up to 10,000 items. CVV2 on bank cards. A bank card can keep its CVV2, shown on the card beside the expiry and copyable like every other field. Delete all.
